brief: The Fed held its policy rate at 3.75-4.0%, as expected, but under chair Kevin Warsh the FOMC was not unanimous this time: two members dissented in favor of a hike. The hold matched Handelsbanken's forecast and the consensus, but Warsh's communication was unexpectedly dovish, uncommitted to the hike his FOMC colleagues had signaled as appropriate this year, and resembling the disastrous July FOMC delivery. That raised the risk of a dovish policy mistake. Markets responded with yield curve steepening (lower front end, higher long end) and a weaker dollar, and Handelsbanken expects FOMC members to try to walk back the move. Handelsbanken still expects a December hike, arguing GDP growth will stay healthy and the labor market will strengthen, further underpinning inflation, even though Warsh says he is unable and unwilling to call financial conditions tight, a reading Handelsbanken shares. Separately, the FOMC will cut its number of policy meetings starting next autumn, to 7 in 2027 and 6 in 2028.
